div.head: VI As 4
div.ab: Quartum: ut omnis homo sit alii coadiutor et inuestigando et coequitando eorum qui bannum hoc audiant, quamdiu uestigium sciatur. Et postquam uestigium deerit, inueniatur semper de duabus decimis unus homo, ubi magis populi sit, sic de una decima, ubi minus populi sit, ad equitandum uel eundum, nisi amplius oporteat, ubi maius necesse sit et omnes elegerint.

Feorðe: þæt ælc man wære oðrum gelastfull ge æt spore ge ǽt midráde þara þe þa gebodu gehyrde, swa lánge swa þe man spor wiste. ⁊ syððan him spór burste, þæt man funde ænne man, þær mare folc sig, swa of anre teoðunge, þær læsse folc sy, to ráde oððe to gánge, buton má þurfe, þider þonne mæst þearf sy, ⁊ hig ealle gecwædon.

Feorðe: Þæt ælc man wære oðrum gelastfull ge æt spore ge ǽt midráde þara þe þa gebodu gehyrde, swa lánge swa þe man spor wiste. ⁊ syððan him spór burste, þæt man funde ænne man [swa of II teoðungum], þær mare folc sig, swa of anre teoðunge, þær læsse folc sy, to ráde oððe to gánge, buton má þurfe, þider þonne mæst þearf sy, ⁊ hig ealle gecwædon.

Fourth: Every man who has heard a summons shall help the rest, both by following a trail, and by riding with them so long as the trail can be followed. And after the trail is lost, one man shall be provided [from two tithings] where the population is large; and from one tithing where the population is small — unless more are needed — to proceed on horseback or on foot, in whatever direction there is most need, according to general consent.

Fourthly: that each man of those that heard the summons was to be helpful to the rest both in following the trail and in riding with them, as long as the trail could be seen; and after the trail had been lost, a man was to be procured [from two tithings] where the population was large, from one tithing where it was more sparse—unless more are required—to ride or go on foot whither there is then greatest need, and they have all agreed.

Viertens: dass jedermann von denen, die diese Gebote gehört haben, dem andern behilflich sei, sowohl bei Spurfolge wie bei Mitritt, so lange wie der Mann [der Vieh verloren hat] die Spur kennt. Und sobald ihm der Spurfaden zerreisst, dass man [ihm je] Einen Mann stelle (von 2 Zehntschaften Quadr.), wo stärkere Bevölkerung ist, oder von Einer Zehntschaft, wo weniger Bevölkerung ist, zum Ritt oder Gehen [in Spursuche], ausser wenn mehr nöthig sind, dorthin, wo es zumeist nöthig ist und sie alle bestimmen.

Fourthly: that everyone of those who have heard these commands help the other, both in following the track and in riding along, as long as the man [who has lost cattle] knows the track. And as soon as the trail breaks off for him, that one man be provided [for him] (from 2 tithings, Quadr.) where the population is larger, or from one tithing where the population is smaller, to ride or go [in search], unless more are needed, [to go] there where there is most need and they all decide.
div.note: Liebermann would supply ‘swa of II teoðungum’ in H from Quadr.
